title: LEGO Ideas Sea Serpent GWP sells out in hours in Australia
summary: The free-with-purchase 40912 Sea Serpent vanished from LEGO.com in Australia and New Zealand just 10 hours into a planned six-day run, sparking questions over whether the UK and other regions will run out too.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO Ideas 40912 Sea Serpent, the gift-with-purchase remake of the 1992 Black Knights set 6057 Sea Serpent, sold out on LEGO.com in Australia and New Zealand roughly 10 hours after launch, despite the promotion being scheduled to run for six days. It's a timed GWP tied to LEGO Insiders Days, which continues until 12 July.

As of writing, the set is still officially available in the UK, US and Europe, where it's included free with qualifying orders over £160 / $180 / €180. That spend threshold covers sets already discounted for Insiders Days, plus double-points themes such as Marvel, Harry Potter, Speed Champions, Jurassic World, Disney, Sonic the Hedgehog, Wicked and LEGO Education.

Whether other regions will follow Australia and sell out early is not confirmed - this is speculation rather than official news, so UK fans should treat any prediction of an early UK sellout as a rumour for now.

## Why it matters
LEGO Castle fans have had slim pickings outside the BrickLink Designer Program lately, so 40912 Sea Serpent has generated strong demand. If you're hoping to grab it in the UK, acting sooner rather than later during Insiders Days seems sensible given how quickly Australian stock disappeared.

## What to watch next
Most of the build can be recreated using your own parts, Pick a Brick or BrickLink if you miss out - the only genuinely exclusive pieces are two new Black Knights shields and the fabric sail, the latter being trickier to substitute convincingly.

title: The LEGO sets that use light bricks best, according to Brick Fanatics
summary: A new feature rounds up seven official LEGO sets that make standout use of the classic light brick, from an X-ray effect in City Hospital to a hidden portrait scare in Haunted House.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Brick Fanatics has published a feature highlighting seven official LEGO sets that make particularly clever use of the light brick element, the small electronic piece that's been part of LEGO sets since the modern 2x3 version launched in 2006.

The roundup was prompted by the newly revealed LEGO Ideas set 21370 E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, which reportedly uses the light brick effectively, though full detail on that model wasn't covered in the excerpt.

Highlights from the list include:

- **76467 Luna Lovegood's House** (764 pieces, released January 2026, currently available) – uses the light brick behind a trans-clear piece to create a shadow-puppet style storytelling effect based on the Deathly Hallows tale.
- **60204 City Hospital** (861 pieces, released 2018, now retired) – hides the light brick behind a translucent panel to mimic an X-ray machine, revealing a skeletal graphic at the press of a button.
- **10273 Haunted House** (3,231 pieces, released 2020, now retired) – conceals the light behind a portrait, with a printed layer creating a spooky glowing reveal.
- **21335 Motorised Lighthouse** (2,065 pieces, released 2022, now retired) – also included in the list, though further detail wasn't available in the source excerpt.

The feature suggests more entries follow beyond these four, but the full list wasn't fully captured in the available text.

## Why it matters
Light bricks are a small but much-loved feature among LEGO builders, often turning a static display into something with genuine wow factor. This kind of roundup is handy for collectors hunting for sets with strong lighting effects, whether for display shelves or nostalgic play value, and it's a reminder that some of the best examples (like City Hospital and Haunted House) are now retired and may be harder to find at retail.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for more detail on how the upcoming 21370 E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial set uses its light brick feature, as this was cited as the inspiration for the roundup but wasn't fully detailed in the available source material.

title: LEGO says Formula 1 is a top priority as motorsport range expands
summary: A senior LEGO executive has said Formula 1 is playing a hugely significant role in the company's portfolio, with more activations and sets expected after the official 2024 partnership launch.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Speaking to motorsport outlet The Race, LEGO Group chief product and marketing officer Julia Goldin confirmed that Formula 1 is now one of the company's most important themes, describing it as playing "a very significant role" in the wider LEGO portfolio.

The LEGO Group and Formula 1 officially confirmed their partnership in 2024, though LEGO has produced F1-inspired sets since the 1970s and has previously worked with individual teams like Williams, Ferrari and McLaren. Since the 2024 deal, the collaboration has expanded well beyond boxed sets, including full-size LEGO cars built for the 2025 Miami Grand Prix, LEGO trophies presented at the 2025 British Grand Prix, and a LEGO Minicar Drivers' Parade at last weekend's British Grand Prix.

Goldin highlighted that F1 sets appeal to a notably broad audience. She noted the theme performs strongly among teen girls and women, tying into F1's own fanbase, which the sport says is 42% female globally, with three in four new fans being women. Popular releases cited include the 43023 McLaren Mastercard F1 Team Lando Norris Helmet, 42240 Aston Martin Aramco AMR25 F1 Car, and 11375 Ferrari F2004 & Michael Schumacher.

## Why it matters
For UK fans and collectors, this signals that LEGO's F1 range is set to keep growing rather than being a short-term crossover. More sets, more team collaborations, and more real-world activations likely mean more collectible releases and potential retail exclusives to watch for.

## What to watch next
Expect further official announcements around future Grand Prix events and possibly new team or driver-branded sets, though no specific upcoming releases have been confirmed yet.

title: LEGO Icons 11374 Arcade Pinball Machine: An Expert Review
summary: The Brothers Brick's resident pinball builder gives a hands-on verdict on the new LEGO Icons Arcade Pinball Machine, out for Insiders now and everyone else from 4 July.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
The Brothers Brick has published a review of the official LEGO Icons 11374 Arcade Pinball Machine, written by a reviewer with personal experience building fully functional LEGO pinball machines. The 2,274-piece set is already available to LEGO Insiders, with a wider release confirmed for 4 July. Pricing is confirmed at USD $229.99 / CAD $319.99 / UK £189.99. The review covers first impressions of the box art, parts, instructions and sticker sheet, with the reviewer noting mixed initial feelings about the colour scheme that improved once the model was built.

## Why it matters
Arcade and pinball-themed sets have proven popular with LEGO Icons fans, following sets like PAC-MAN Arcade and the smaller Arcade Machine. A detailed review from someone with genuine pinball-building expertise gives potential buyers useful insight into build quality and play features before committing to the purchase price.

## What to watch next
The reviewer hints that the "Arcade" naming could suggest more arcade-themed sets may follow, though this is speculation on their part rather than confirmed by LEGO. Fans interested in the set should watch for the full release on 4 July and further impressions once more builders get hands-on.

title: Fan builder recreates Tokyo's Nakagin Capsule Tower in LEGO bricks
summary: Builder Ids de Jong has completed a striking LEGO tribute to Tokyo's demolished Nakagin Capsule Tower, first shown at Skaerbaek Fan Weekend and now fully photographed.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Fan builder Ids de Jong has finished a large custom LEGO model of Tokyo's iconic Nakagin Capsule Tower, the modular building that stood in the city until it was demolished a few years ago. According to The Brothers Brick, the model debuted at Skaerbaek Fan Weekend last year, and new photos of the completed build have now been shared.

The MOC leans into a moody, sci-fi lighting style, lit from multiple angles to give it a dystopian, cyberpunk feel — a look often seen in LEGO builds inspired by Japanese architecture and design. Ids has kept the model recognisable by mirroring real details from the original tower, including the distinctive angular, dark-toned capsule sections and brick-built Japanese signage. Sharp-eyed fans may also spot some printed parts reused from an early LEGO Star Wars set.

This is a fan-made creation (MOC) and is not an official LEGO Group set or product.

## Why it matters
Architectural MOCs like this show how far fan builders can push realism and lighting techniques to recreate real-world buildings, especially ones that no longer exist. For stadium, display, and architecture build fans, it's a good example of how texture, colour blocking, and printed parts can bring a striking real structure to life in brick form.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for more photos or a build breakdown from Ids de Jong, and watch for similar architectural MOCs at future fan events like Skaerbaek Fan Weekend.

title: Builder Bricktopher Brings Star Wars to Life in Microscale
summary: Fan builder Bricktopher has created a series of microscale Star Wars scenes, from Naboo's Theed to the Battle of Hoth, showcasing clever part use and scale.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
A builder known as Bricktopher has shared a set of microscale Star Wars creations, as featured by The Brothers Brick. The scenes include Theed on Naboo (complete with tiny N1 Starfighters built from Technic bushes, a T-bar and a minifig hand), the Death Star trench run, a Star Destroyer looming over Jedha, a Battle of Hoth vignette with Snowspeeders and AT-AT segments, and the destruction of Tipoca City on Kamino.

Each build leans into clever part usage — from hidden studs for a clean 'model kit' look to hairpieces standing in for laser fire — to capture iconic moments from the films in a compact scale.

## Why it matters
Microscale building is a great way to showcase big cinematic moments without needing huge amounts of space or parts, and this collection is a good example of creative part reuse and scene composition for anyone interested in display builds, custom models or Star Wars-themed brick projects.

## What to watch next
Fans of these builds may want to keep an eye on Bricktopher's future work or similar microscale Star Wars creations shared across the brick-building community.

title: Fan-built LEGO Meduseld brings Rohan's Golden Hall to life
summary: Builder monsieur.kek has created a striking MOC of Meduseld, the Golden Hall of Rohan from Lord of the Rings, filling a gap left since the 2012 Helm's Deep sets.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Fan builder monsieur.kek has unveiled a large-scale custom LEGO model (MOC) of Meduseld, the Golden Hall of King Théoden from The Lord of the Rings. According to The Brothers Brick, the build uses SNOT (studs not on top) techniques to create wood-effect pillars and walls, stacked cheese slopes for texture beneath the golden arches, and a tan tiled roof echoing the style seen on the official LEGO Rivendell set.

The model includes custom minifigures of King Théoden - using the hair piece from the new Unicorn Elf collectible minifigure - and Éowyn, a character rarely seen in minifig form. The whole build sits on an elevated stone platform designed for minifig display.

This is a fan creation, not an official LEGO Group set.

## Why it matters
The official LEGO Lord of the Rings range has recently expanded with Minas Tirith, but Rohirrim-themed sets have been thin on the ground since 2012's Helm's Deep and Uruk-Hai Army. This MOC shows how the fan community is filling that gap with impressive scale and detail, and offers inspiration for anyone wanting to build their own Middle-earth display pieces.

## What to watch next
No word yet on official LEGO plans for more Rohan-themed sets, but fan interest in this era of Middle-earth could be a hint at demand LEGO might eventually respond to.

title: BrickLink Designer Program to change again for 2028 submissions
summary: BrickLink has confirmed fresh changes to its Designer Program, with the first round of 2028 submissions opening this autumn.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
BrickLink has officially confirmed that its BrickLink Designer Program (BDP) is changing again, with the new format kicking off when the first 2028 submission window opens this Fall.

The BDP has a history of evolving. It grew out of an earlier AFOL Designer Program from 2018, before BrickLink (working with LEGO Group as its parent company) launched the BDP proper in 2021. That first version ran as three rounds of crowd-funded competitions between LEGO Ideas sets that narrowly missed out on the official 10k club threshold.

The program was then relaunched in early 2024 with a different structure: multiple curated submission rounds each year from fan designers, working within a limited part and colour palette and strict submission rules.

Brickset notes that change has been a constant theme of the program so far, and this latest update continues that pattern ahead of 2028. The full details of what's changing weren't fully outlined in the available source material, so exact rule changes should be checked directly with BrickLink before being reported as confirmed specifics.

## Why it matters
The BDP is one of the main routes for fan designers to get original creations turned into official, buildable sets through BrickLink. Any changes to submission rules, timing or format directly affect AFOL creators, Ideas fans and collectors who follow the program's output each year.

## What to watch next
Brick fans should keep an eye on BrickLink's own channels for the full breakdown of the new 2028 rules, including submission windows, part palettes and eligibility criteria, once they're published in full.

title: LEGO Insiders Days promotions now live, including free Sea Serpent set
summary: LEGO's annual Insiders Days event has kicked off on LEGO.com, bringing gifts-with-purchase, double points on selected themes and regional discounts.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO's yearly Insiders Days promotions are now running on LEGO.com. UK shoppers spending over £160 can add 40912 Sea Serpent to their basket as a free gift, while a £90 spend on Creator, City or Friends sets unlocks the 5010033 Airplane – Special Edition as a bonus build.

On top of the gifts-with-purchase, several themes are earning double Insiders points for the duration of the promotion, including Sonic the Hedgehog, Jurassic World, Speed Champions, Harry Potter, Marvel, Disney, Wicked and Education sets.

Discounts are also part of the event, though these vary by region. European examples flagged so far include 20% off 10323 PAC-MAN Arcade and a discount on 10337 Lamborghini, with more reductions likely to appear as the promotion continues.

## Why it matters
Insiders Days is one of the bigger recurring promotional windows on LEGO.com, and free GWP sets like the Sea Serpent tend to be popular with collectors who like completing themed extras. Double points events are also a handy way to boost your Insiders rewards balance ahead of future redemptions.

## What to watch next
Exact discount lists and thresholds can differ between the UK, US and EU stores, so it's worth checking LEGO.com directly for your region's current offers, and keeping an eye out for further set-specific discounts as the promotion rolls on.

title: LEGO Pokémon range grows with first-ever minifigures
summary: The LEGO Group and The Pokémon Company International have officially confirmed five new LEGO Pokémon sets, including a Poké Ball set that introduces the first LEGO Pokémon minifigures.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
The LEGO Group and The Pokémon Company International have officially announced five new additions to the LEGO Pokémon range, which launched in March with a series of large-scale buildable creatures. According to the confirmed press release, the new wave includes further creature-style builds alongside a Poké Ball set that, for the first time, features LEGO Pokémon minifigures and Pokémon figures.

Exact set numbers, pricing and full contents haven't been detailed in the excerpt available, but the announcement confirms this is an expansion of the existing LEGO Pokémon build-and-display line rather than a rumoured concept.

## Why it matters
Minifigures are a huge part of what makes LEGO collectable and displayable, so their arrival in the Pokémon range is a significant step for the theme. It signals LEGO and The Pokémon Company International see long-term potential here, likely opening the door to more sets, characters and trainer-style builds down the line — good news for collectors and display builders alike.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for official set numbers, images and pricing as LEGO typically follows these press announcements with retailer listings. It's also worth watching whether more minifigures or trainer characters get added to future waves.
